title: UAE Cabinet approves Executive Regulations of Federal Decree-Law on Entry and Residence of Foreigners
contains: WAM, 18 Apr 2022: Cabinet approves the executive regulation of the entry and residence decree-law: 10-year golden residence for investors, entrepreneurs (AED 1 million revenue or a project sold for AED 7 million), talents, scientists, professionals (AED 30,000 salary), students, humanitarian pioneers, frontline heroes; family sponsorship regardless of age, no limit on time abroad; real-estate route AED 2 million incl. bank loans and off-plan; 5-year green residence for skilled employees (AED 15,000), freelancers (AED 360,000), investors/partners (replacing a 2-year permit); visit visas (5-year tourist visa, USD 4,000 balance, 90/180 days); grace periods up to 6 months; in force 90 days after publication. Investor golden terms and the event are recorded; entrepreneur, talent and other visa criteria are out of scope.

II 39/2014 (3 pages, authentic signed copy) on the procedure for a § 10(6) StbG confirmation: Land government forwards the file to the Interior Ministry only once § 10(1) Z 2-6 and 8 and (2) are met (§ 1); Interior Ministry passes the reasoned application to the competent minister(s), and to the Foreign Ministry when the applicant has no main residence in Austria; ministers give reasoned opinions and may consult experts (§ 2); Interior Ministry prepares a recommendation (§ 3); the government decides regularly, at least once every calendar half-year (§ 4); decisions are sent to the Land (§ 5); in force at the end of the day of publication, 28 Feb 2014 (§ 7). No amounts, fees, economic thresholds or counts. Already in the data: the rule_change event e-aa4d9ac83f (2014-02-28). Nothing further in scope.

title: Staatsbürgerschaftsgesetz 1985 (StbG), § 10, consolidated version in force from 12.06.2026 (last amended by BGBl. I Nr. 39/2026)
contains: Consolidated text of § 10 StbG 1985 in force from 12 Jun 2026 (RIS page, with list of earlier versions back to 1985): general naturalisation conditions (§ 10(1): ten years' lawful residence of which five settled, no convictions, secured livelihood etc.; (2) bars; (3) renunciation of former nationality; (5) livelihood test averaged over 36 months of the last six years) and the constitutional provision § 10(6): the federal government's confirmation of extraordinary past and expected achievements in the special interest of the Republic waives § 10(1) Z 1 (residence) and Z 7 (livelihood) and § 10(3) (renunciation); § 10(7) allows a procedural regulation (BGBl. II 39/2014). No amounts, fees or counts for the programme; the residence and income numbers are conditions of ordinary naturalisation that § 10(6) waives, so they are not terms of this programme. The version list is about § 10 as a whole, not § 10(6) (whose wording per the source notes is unchanged), so no events added.

Events (2013 fast-track, 2022 repeal) were already in the data; the holding periods, notification deadline and the ordinary 5-year route now added as terms.

title: Законопроект за изменение на Закона за българското гражданство, № 47-202-01-2, с мотиви и Решение № 12 на Министерския съвет от 14 януари 2022 г. (Government bi
contains: Bill file 47-202-01-2 sent to the National Assembly (cover letter dated '18.01.2021', evidently 2022; Council of Ministers Decision No. 12 of 14 Jan 2022; draft law; motives). Draft: repeal arts. 12a and 14a, related amendments, and a transitional rule that pending applications be decided under the old rules (the law as adopted instead terminated them). Motives: Commission report of 23 Jan 2019; residence periods before naturalisation (5 years art. 12a, 1 year art. 14a, 3 years for the investor's spouse) while investors stayed only days or weeks; most applicants held government securities or trust deposits over BGN 1 million, raised to BGN 2 million, often sold before naturalisation; checks hindered by bank and tax secrecy; the 2019 government bill and Parliament's 2021 choice to keep the scheme with more control; Commission letter of June 2021; no budget impact. The annexes listed (impact assessment, consultation reports) are not in this file. No statistics. Bill approval was already an event; residence periods, the BGN 1 million thresholds and three dated events now added.

contains: Law 140 of 2019 (30 July 2019), law-firm transcription: Art. 1 replaces Art. 17 of the Aliens Law 89/1960 (three residence categories, i.e. drops the deposit-residence category); Art. 2 replaces Nationality Law Art. 4 bis (Prime Minister may naturalise foreigners who buy state property, set up an investment project, or pay foreign currency to the Treasury or as a Central Bank deposit, per a PM decree); Art. 3 adds Art. 4 bis 1 (Cabinet unit with members from Foreign Affairs, Interior, Investment and security agencies) and 4 bis 2 (USD 10,000 fee, confidentiality option, initial decision within 3 months, 6 months' temporary residence, final recommendation within 3 months); Art. 4 repeals Art. 20 bis of Law 89/1960; Art. 5 entry into force. title: القانون رقم 173 لسنة 2018 بتعديل بعض أحكام القانون رقم 89 لسنة 1960 بشأن دخول وإقامة الأجانب والقانون رقم 26 لسنة 1975 بشأن الجنسية المصرية (Law No. 173 of 2018
contains: Text of Law 173/2018 (Official Gazette No. 32 bis (b), 14 Aug 2018) as transcribed by an Egyptian law firm's website, in four articles: Art. 1 replaces Art. 17 of Law 89/1960 to add a fourth residence category, 'deposit residence'; Art. 2 adds Art. 20 bis defining it (foreigners coming to invest who deposit at least EGP 7 million, or the foreign-currency equivalent set by PM decree, in an Egyptian bank; conditions, duration, deposit rules, banks and investment fields to be set by Interior Minister decree after Cabinet approval); Art. 3 adds Art. 4 bis to Nationality Law 26/1975 (Interior Minister may naturalise a deposit-residence foreigner after 5 consecutive years' residence before applying, if conditions 1-3 of Art. 4(4) are met; the deposit then passes to the Treasury; Art. 9 restrictions apply; application rules by Interior Minister decree); Art. 4 in force the day after publication. Rest of the page is the law firm's menus. The one image is the firm's logo (no text to OCR). No counts or fees. The EGP 7 million minimum is already term t-30e8d343de (whose notes carry the 5-year and Treasury rules) and the publication/entry into force is event e-5f23bfc145; nothing further in scope. No naturalised persons named.

title: Ley 14/2013, de 27 de septiembre, de apoyo a los emprendedores y su internacionalización (BOE-A-2013-10074)
contains: Full text of Ley 14/2013 (BOE 28 Sep 2013, 96 pp.): support for entrepreneurs, tax and internationalisation measures (out of scope), and Title V Section 2 'Movilidad internacional' (arts. 61-76 and additional provisions). In scope: investor visa and residence authorisation (arts. 61-67): route thresholds (5 existing terms) and launch event (existing); now added the other rules as terms (visa validity, initial and renewal durations, 60-day investment window, 5-year public-debt holding, one-trip presence rule, 90-day visa grace period, certificate dating (30/90 days), minimum age 18, criminal-record look-back 5 years, family members (children under 18), stay-visa validity up to 5 years, absences over six months tolerated at renewal (DA 6.ª), investment through a company) and statutory deadlines as processing_time_goal_days (visa 10 working days, authorisation 20 days, police check 7 days). Fees are left to a ministerial order (DF 10.ª.4; no amount printed); DF 11.ª requires an annual report to the Council of Ministers (no numbers). Entrepreneur, highly-qualified, researcher and intra-company rules are out of scope.

Programme content: the first CBI dividend (paid for the first time in the programme's history; about 17,500 people reached in its inaugural round; paid to Social Security contributors); 2022 non-tax revenue 54.9% above budget mainly because of CBI proceeds (no CBI amount); CBI section (paras 51-53): real estate option minimum US$400,000, mandatory applicant interviews and the Sustainable Island State Contribution introduced, enhanced due diligence; medium-term plan to reduce reliance on CBI revenue and to explore saving part of it in a dedicated fund. No CBI revenue amount is printed. The rest (macro outlook, sector policies, debt, social programmes, worker bonus) is out of scope.

title: 2025 Budget Address (Prime Minister and Minister of Finance)
contains: 2025 Budget Address (16 Dec 2024, 58 pages). Programme content: 2023 non-tax revenue 18.7% above budget mainly from CBI proceeds and 2024 revenue 22.6% below the approved estimates mainly from lower CBI contributions (no CBI amounts; these percentages are about total revenue, not CBI, so not recorded); CIU restructured into a statutory body (1 October 2024; already an event from this source) with claims of increased applications and record revenue (no figures); milestones including a ten-week target for application decisions and a 24-hour response time (recorded as an event; the ten weeks are not recorded under processing_time_months, which is in months); SISC and Public Benefit Option described, real-estate thresholds reduced (no amounts); two CBI dividends paid; programme claimed to rank first in the world in 2024 (industry ranking, out of scope). The rest is out of scope.

title: 2026 Budget Address (Prime Minister and Minister of Finance)
contains: 2026 Budget Address (16 Dec 2025, 53 pages). Programme content: 2025 non-tax revenue 48.3% below budget because of a CBI slowdown, and 2025 total revenue projected about 31.3% below the approved estimates largely because of CBI shortfall (already an event from this source; percentages are about total or non-tax revenue, not recorded); budgetary support to the Nevis Island Administration despite lower CBI revenue; CIU section (paras 48-50): blockchain-verified due diligence certification, Saturn digital platform, role in setting up the Eastern Caribbean CBI Regulatory Authority (new event), top of the CBI Index for a fifth year and awards (industry rankings, out of scope), an Investment Gateway Summit with close to 200 citizens and investors (out of scope), a CIU Micro and Small Business Grant Programme of EC$10,000 each to 36 businesses (in the event description; no total printed, so no observation). No CBI revenue amount is printed. The rest is out of scope.

title: Canada accords partial visa waiver to citizens of St. Kitts and Nevis
contains: SKNIS relay of a Prime Minister's Office statement (6 June 2023): Canada partially lifts the visa requirement imposed on St Kitts and Nevis nationals in 2014; those who held a Canadian visa in the past ten years or hold a current US non-immigrant visa can apply for an eTA; others still need a visa. Already recorded as a visa_access event from this source; no numbers about the programme (the ten-year look-back is a condition, not a statistic).

title: Ordonnance Souveraine n° 3.153 du 19 mars 1964 relative aux conditions d'entrée et de séjour des étrangers dans la Principauté (consolidated)
contains: Consolidated Sovereign Ordinance 3.153 of 19 March 1964 on entry and stay of foreigners in Monaco (Legimonaco): passport and French entry conditions, residence card application within 8 days (over 16), housing proof, card types (temporary up to 1 year; ordinary after 3 years, valid 3 years; Monegasque spouse card 5 years; privileged after 10 years, valid 10 years), conditions (work permit or sufficient means), lodging registration by hotels and landlords, sanctions (fines in old francs) and expulsion. No minimum amount of money; validity and qualifying periods added as terms; the 1964 ordinance recorded as the launch event (programs.csv already gives 1964-03-19). No statistics.

title: Hotărâre cu privire la aprobarea proiectului de lege pentru instituirea moratoriului privind acordarea cetățeniei Republicii Moldova în condițiile art. 17 alin.
contains: Draft Government decision (Feb 2020, PM Ion Chicu) approving a bill for a moratorium until 1 Jan 2021 on new applications under art. 17(11)-(12) of Citizenship Law 1024/2000 (citizenship by investment); pending applications to be examined as set by the Government; 2019 contracts of accredited agents extended by the moratorium period without the fee of annex 3 pt. 4 of HG 786/2017; informative note (Ministry of Economy and Infrastructure: a repeated moratorium to allow a final decision on the programme; no extra budget cost). No numbers. Covered by event e-5e85d6b6b2.

title: Proiectul hotărârii de Guvern cu privire la modificarea Hotărârii Guvernului nr. 786 din 04.10.2017 cu privire la dobândirea cetățeniei prin investiție (draft,
contains: Consultation draft (Word, 20 Mar 2018) amending Government Decision 786/2017 on citizenship by investment: due diligence by a company contracted by the Commission; reputation checks extended to dependent family members aged 16 or more (draft pt. 7^1); applications via an information system or the Commission secretariat; Commission to select by tender an exclusive company to design, implement and promote the programme for up to 5 years, extendable by up to 3, paid by applicants through a commission, no public money; bidder criteria (at least 5 years of CBI experience, forecasts of programme investment, free application and due-diligence IT systems); programme start within 3 months of the contract. Draft provisions, not confirmed as adopted, so not recorded as programme terms; covered by event e-5eca14bc42. No statistics.

title: Lineamientos para trámites y procedimientos migratorios (Secretaría de Gobernación), DOF 8 November 2012
contains: DOF text of the 2012 Lineamientos para trámites y procedimientos migratorios (Secretaría de Gobernación): definitions and general rules, then procedure sheets (fichas) for visas, entry, status changes, regularisation, permanent residence, documents, with fees by reference to the Ley Federal de Derechos (no amounts printed), maximum decision times and validity. In scope: the investor case for temporary residence (shareholding or business fixed assets worth 20,000 days of minimum wage, or business with at least five formal jobs; repeated in arts. 41, 43, 52), the real-estate case (40,000 days), validity (1-3 years on change of status, up to 4 years) and decision times (20 working days). The investor amount was already recorded; real estate, jobs, validity and processing time added. Economic-solvency cases (bank balances of 20,000 days or income of 400 days a month), employment offers, students and invitations are not investment routes and are not recorded. No statistics. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

title: North Macedonia 2025 Report, SWD(2025) 753 final
contains: European Commission North Macedonia 2025 Report (SWD(2025) 753, 105 pp.): the whole accession assessment (political criteria, economy, all chapters). Programme content is one paragraph under Chapter 23 'Citizenship rights' (PDF p. 45): the Commission's view that special-economic-interest citizenship must not be granted systematically, and grants of economic citizenship to two Turkish nationals in 2024 and one national of Bosnia and Herzegovina in 2025. Both numbers are already in the data. Other mentions of the Visa Suspension Mechanism, visa policy (Türkiye visa waiver), online citizenship certificates and FDI are not about the programme. Nothing new to add. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

title: Screening report North Macedonia, Cluster 1 - Fundamentals (external version)
contains: European Commission screening report, Cluster 1 Fundamentals (130 pp.), covering judiciary, fundamental rights, justice/freedom/security, public procurement, statistics, financial control and public administration. Programme content (repeated on p. 68, Chapter 23 'EU citizenship rights', and p. 90, Chapter 24 visa policy): description of the investor citizenship procedure (Interior Ministry drafts, Finance and Economy ministries assess the economic interest, security agency checks, Government decides), 121 people naturalised for economic reasons 2005-2022 against 40 negative decisions, the December 2012 amendment, and the recommendation to refrain from systematic investor citizenship. All already in the data (two observations, one event). Nothing new to add. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

title: Уредба за утврдување на критериумите за особен научен, економски, културен, спортски или друг национален интерес за стекнување на државјанство на Република Маке
contains: Official Gazette no. 9/2005 (9 Feb 2005), whole issue. Programme content is item 146: the Government decree of 7 Feb 2005 on criteria for special scientific, economic, cultural, sporting or other national interest (Art. 3: economic interest through direct investment, donation, securities, shares, know-how, innovation, new technologies, or as top manager, expert, trade partner, donor for economic reforms, etc.; no minimum amount; assessed by the Ministries of Economy and Finance), in force the day after publication. The rest of the issue (consumer council fees, summer time, gambling revenue, appointments, budget programmes) is unrelated. The decree is already an event; it sets no amount, so no term row (the existing EUR 400,000 term notes that there was no minimum before 20 Dec 2012).

title: Уредба за изменување и дополнување на Уредбата за утврдување на критериумите за особен ... национален интерес за стекнување на државјанство, Службен весник бр.
contains: Official Gazette no. 161/2012 (19 Dec 2012), whole issue. Programme content is item 3852: decree amendment of 6 Dec 2012 rewriting Art. 3 (EUR 400,000 per person direct investment in new capacity, excluding catering and retail, with at least 10 open-ended employees for at least one year; documents the Ministry of Finance checks; the other non-amount economic criteria kept). In force the day after publication. Already recorded as one term and one event; the rest of the issue is unrelated.

title: Уредба за изменување на Уредбата за утврдување на критериумите за особен ... национален интерес за стекнување на државјанство, Службен весник на РСМ бр. 255/201
contains: Official Gazette of RNM no. 255/2019 (13 Dec 2019), whole issue. Programme content is the decree amendment of 10 Dec 2019: renames the country in the decree and rewrites Art. 3, keeping the EUR 400,000 / 10-jobs route and adding a EUR 200,000 per person, two-year investment in a private investment fund (fund with at least EUR 5,000,000 initial capital, investing in the economy or innovation and not in real estate, at most 500 foreign applicant-investors), assessed by the Fund for Innovation and Technology Development on listed documents. In force the day after publication. Already recorded as one term (with the fund conditions in its notes) and one event; the re-enacted EUR 400,000 route is covered by the 2012 term. The rest of the issue is unrelated.

title: Уредба за дополнување на Уредбата за утврдување на критериумите за особен ... национален интерес за стекнување државјанство, Службен весник на РСМ бр. 42/2021
contains: Official Gazette of RNM no. 42/2021 (19 Feb 2021), whole issue. Programme content is item 624: decree amendment of 16 Feb 2021 adding a scientific-interest criterion (doctorate, at least six papers in five years, led at least one research project), requiring the Fund for Innovation and Technology Development to adopt a rulebook and a fee tariff for the economic-interest procedure with Government consent (no fee amount given), and adding literature to the cultural criteria; in force on the eighth day after publication. Already an event; no amounts. The rest of the issue is unrelated.

title: Закон за државјанството на Република Македонија (Law on Citizenship), Службен весник на Република Македонија бр. 67/1992
contains: Official Gazette no. 67/1992 (Tuesday 3 Nov 1992), whole issue: Law on Citizenship adopted by the Assembly on 27 Oct 1992 (in force on the eighth day after publication), plus the Law on travel documents and other items. Programme content: Art. 11 (adult foreigner may be naturalised by exception from Art. 7 where of special scientific, economic, cultural or national interest; Government gives prior opinion; spouse may also be naturalised under Art. 9 conditions); Art. 12 (minor children naturalised with parents); Art. 14 (annulment for false data). General naturalisation conditions (15 years' residence etc.) and the passport law are context, not programme numbers. Already one event (dated to year 1992); no amounts or statistics.

title: Закон за изменување и дополнување на Законот за државјанството на Република Македонија, Службен весник бр. 8/2004
contains: Official Gazette no. 8/2004 (23 Feb 2004), whole issue: Law amending the Law on Citizenship, adopted 22 Jan 2004, in force on the eighth day after publication. Programme content: Art. 8 rewrites Art. 11 (applicant must meet Art. 7(1) points 1 and 8, i.e. adult and no security threat; special scientific, economic, cultural, sporting or other national interest; Government to set criteria by decree). Other changes (8 years' ordinary residence, oath, guarantee of admission, ex-Yugoslav transitional rule) concern ordinary naturalisation. Already one event; no amounts or statistics.

title: Act No. XXI of 2025, Maltese Citizenship (Amendment) Act, 2025
contains: Act XXI of 2025 (assented 24 Jul 2025, passed 23 Jul 2025) amending the Maltese Citizenship Act: deletes the individual investor programme definition, rewrites art. 10(9) as naturalisation by merit, renames regulator complaint provisions, and new art. 27(4) keeping applications filed before entry into force under the old rules. Also citizenship-by-descent dates moved to 1 Aug 2028 and adoption rules (out of scope). No programme numbers; the event is already in events.

title: Judgment of the Court (Grand Chamber) of 29 April 2025, European Commission v Republic of Malta, Case C-181/23
contains: CJEU Grand Chamber judgment of 29 Apr 2025 in C-181/23 (EUR-Lex HTML page). Legal framework (Treaty articles, Maltese Citizenship Act art. 10, IIP 2014 cap of 1,800, 2020 regulations: EUR 600,000/750,000 contribution, EUR 10,000 deposit, EUR 700,000 property or EUR 16,000 rent, EUR 10,000 donation, 36/12 months residence, EUR 50,000 per dependant, cap of 400 a year and 1,500 in total), pre-litigation timeline (1 Apr 2020 letter, 20 Oct 2020 formal notice, Malta's replies of 18 Dec 2020, 6 Aug 2021 and 6 Jun 2022, 9 Jun 2021 additional notice, 2 Mar 2022 suspension for Russians and Belarusians, 6 Apr 2022 reasoned opinion), parties' arguments, findings and costs. The fee and cap figures repeat L.N. 437 of 2020 and are already in program_terms and events from that source, so not repeated. Added: events for the 1 Apr 2020 Commission letter, the 28 Jul 2020 act and the 21 Mar 2023 filing (other dates already in events). Malta's procedural replies and the hearing date are court procedure, not programme changes. No statistics. For decision: para 36 also lists ten nationalities still excluded from the 2020 scheme (Afghanistan, DR Congo, Iran, North Korea, Somalia, South Sudan, Sudan, Syria, Venezuela, Yemen); the existing 2022-03-02 event (same source) could mention this in its description.

title: Press Release No 52/25: Judgment of the Court in Case C-181/23 | Commission v Malta (Citizenship by investment)
contains: CJEU Press Release No 52/25 (29 Apr 2025) summarising the judgment in C-181/23 that the 2020 investor citizenship scheme infringes Art. 20 TFEU and Art. 4(3) TEU. No numbers. The judgment event is already in events (from the judgment itself).

title: Amendments to the Maltese Citizenship Act and subsidiary legislation
contains: Komunita Malta notice of 2 Sep 2025 listing Act XXI of 2025 (in force 24 Jul 2025) and L.N. 159 of 2025 (merit-based naturalisation rules); also mentions the citizenship-by-descent deadline extension and adoption clarification (out of scope). No numbers. The event is already in events.

title: Press Release: The Government publishes amendments to the Maltese Citizenship Act
contains: Komunita Malta press release of 23 Jul 2025: amendments to the Citizenship Act to comply with CJEU C-181/23, discontinuing the Granting of Citizenship for Exceptional Services programme and removing references to the transaction and agents; minister and lawyer quotes. No numbers. The event is already in events.

title: Investor citizenship schemes: European Commission opens infringements against Cyprus and Malta for "selling" EU citizenship (IP/20/1925)
contains: European Commission press release of 20 Oct 2020 opening infringement procedures (letters of formal notice) against Cyprus and Malta over investor citizenship schemes; background on the 2019 report, the April 2020 letters and the July 2020 Parliament resolution; also a letter to Bulgaria. No programme numbers. The Malta event (letter of formal notice) is already in events.

title: Investor citizenship scheme: Commission refers MALTA to the Court of Justice (IP/22/5422)
contains: European Commission press release of 29 Sep 2022 referring Malta to the Court of Justice: timeline (formal notice 20 Oct 2020, additional notice 9 Jun 2021, reasoned opinion 6 Apr 2022, suspension for Russian and Belarusian nationals 2 Mar 2022), the IIP cap of 1,800 successful main applicants (already in the IIP launch event), and notes on Cyprus and Bulgaria. Only unquantified programme figure: "several thousand investors and their family members" naturalised (not a number). All Malta events are already in events.

title: Malta: 2019 Article IV Consultation - Press Release; Staff Report; and Statement by the Executive Director for Malta (IMF Country Report No. 19/68)
contains: IMF Country Report 19/68: Malta 2019 Article IV press release, staff report (macro developments, housing, fiscal, financial sector, AML/CFT, external assessment, DSA) and Executive Director statement. Programme content: IIP proceeds in the fiscal accounts (Table 2 memorandum lines: overall balance, structural balance and structural primary balance excluding IIP proceeds, 2016-2024), the authorities' estimate that IIP export receipts were about 1% of GDP a year in 2015-2017 (Annex IV), qualitative mentions of IIP demand, housing and AML risks, and a DSA stress test without IIP revenue. Already in data: 2015-2017 receipts and overall balance excl. IIP for 2016-2018. Added: overall balance excl. IIP projections 2019-2024 and the two structural series 2016-2024 (two new indicators proposed). The p. 20 text table repeats the same structural figures for 2018-2023 (same source, not repeated). The DSA "IIP proceed shock" (debt 33% of GDP at end of projection, 3 points above baseline) is a debt scenario rather than a programme figure and is not recorded; Figure 3 and the Figure 5 stress-test chart have no printed IIP values. The rest of the report (growth, banks, NIIP, labour) is not about the programme.

title: L.N. 167 of 2013, Global Residence Programme Rules, 2013
contains: L.N. 167 of 2013, Global Residence Programme Rules (in force 1 Jul 2013; English text, the Maltese pages carry no extractable text): definitions, qualifying property thresholds (EUR 275,000 / 220,000 purchase; EUR 9,600 / 8,750 a year rent), application through an authorised registered mandatary with a EUR 6,000 fee (EUR 5,500 for owned property in the south), beneficiary conditions, 15% tax on remitted foreign income with a EUR 15,000 minimum, 35% on other income, cessation (incl. more than 183 days in another jurisdiction, EUR 5,000 penalty for late notification), information exchange, schedule of southern localities. Added the EUR 8,750 rent and EUR 5,500 fee; the other amounts and the start date were already recorded. The tax rates, the late-notification penalty and the 183-day rule are conditions rather than prices and are described here only. No statistics. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

title: L.N. 47 of 2014, Individual Investor Programme of the Republic of Malta Regulations, 2014

title: L.N. 288 of 2015, Malta Residence and Visa Programme Regulations, 2015

title: L.N. 437 of 2020, Granting of Citizenship for Exceptional Services Regulations, 2020
contains: L.N. 437 of 2020, Granting of Citizenship for Exceptional Services Regulations (English text): definitions (dependants incl. children to 29 and parents over 55), general provisions, disqualifications, eligibility assessment with four-tier due diligence, Part III merit route (8 months residence, Evaluation Board), Part IV direct-investment route (36 months residence or 12 with the higher contribution, EUR 700,000 property or EUR 16,000 rent for 5 years, EUR 10,000 donation), cap of 400 a year and 1,500 in total, non-refundable fees, continuing obligations, deprivation, data protection, repeal of the IIP regulations with savings, First Schedule (EUR 600,000 / 750,000 contribution with EUR 10,000 deposit, EUR 50,000 per dependant; due diligence and administrative fees), Second Schedule (residence permit fees), Third and Fourth Schedules (competent bodies, oath). title: L.N. 121 of 2021, Malta Permanent Residence Programme Regulations, 2021

In scope: s. 25 Immigration Act (IHS buyers get resident status: event added; occupation permit for start-up investors, s. 9A(1A)); s. 29 Investment Promotion Act Schedule Part I new items 1E (USD 100,000 incl. high-tech equipment, USD 25,000 transfer) and 1F (USD 40,000 start-ups, 20% R&D) (terms added) and item 6 retired non-citizen USD 2,500 at issue and monthly (already in data); s. 41 Non-Citizens (Property Restriction) Act: retirees may acquire a lifetime right to live in a care home or similar unit outside smart cities (no amount); s. 61 commencement. Land duty and registration duty amendments have no scheme-specific rates. No statistics. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

title: The Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2020 (Act No. 7 of 2020)
contains: Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2020 (74 sections amending many Acts; mostly tax, customs, banking, other matters, not in scope). In scope: s. 16 EDB Act (new First Schedule in Third Schedule: criteria for investors, start-ups, food processing, film studio, other investors, professionals, young professionals, self-employed, retirees; PRP criteria Part II and pre-1 Sep 2020 Part III); s. 27 Immigration Act (USD 375,000 property residence incl. IRS/RES/IHS/PDS/SCS, PRP direct investment USD 375,000, permits 10 years, PRP 20 years, transitional PRP s. 5A(5AB), right of retirees to invest s. 9H); s. 45 Non-Citizens (Property Restriction) (Smart City serviced plots); s. 32 land duty references; s. 74 commencement (ss. 16(f) and 27 from 2 Sep 2020). Terms added for all investor and retiree criteria not already in data; professional and self-employed criteria (salaries, USD 35,000 self-employed) are not investment routes and were not taken. Two events added. Note: the existing FA 2020 terms and the property threshold event use 7 Aug 2020 (Act date) although s. 74(7) gives 2 Sep 2020. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

title: The Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2021 (Act No. 15 of 2021)
contains: Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2021 (97 sections amending many Acts; mostly tax, customs, finance and other matters, not in scope). In scope: s. 22 EDB Act (registration and deregistration rules incl. revocation of permits, Premium Investor Scheme for projects of MUR 500 million (business incentive, not residence), saving for pre-2006 investors, new First Schedule in the Fifth Schedule: investor USD 50,000 options and renewal income, retiree USD 1,500 a month or USD 18,000 a year, PRP criteria (USD 375,000; 3 years plus MUR 15 million; retiree USD 54,000), pre-Sept 2020 and pre-Oct 2006 criteria, Family Occupation Permit USD 250,000 to the COVID-19 Projects Development Fund (already in data)); s. 37 Immigration Act (G+2 apartments USD 375,000 and FOP s. 9CA: already in data with launch event; permits deemed approved after 5 working days; PRP 20 years; retiree PRP conversion USD 1,500 a month). Restated amounts identical to the 2020 schedule were not added again; the 2020 'film studio' and 'any other investor' items were dropped (valid_to set on those 2020 terms). s. 77 Registration Duty Act and s. 44 Land (Duties and Taxes) Act change IRS/RES/IHS duty references and delete USD 50,000/25,000 minimum-duty alternatives without printing the scheme rates (not taken). s. 62 Non-Citizens (Property Restriction) Act: EDB register of non-citizen property. Terms added: decision deadline, PRP conversion income, pre-2006 turnover, FOP validity. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

title: The Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2023 (Act No. 12 of 2023)
contains: Finance (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act 2023 (93 sections amending many Acts; mostly tax, customs and other matters, not in scope). In scope: s. 24 EDB Act (Premium Investor Scheme objects (business incentive); First Schedule: investor USD 50,000 with proof of funds and transfer within 60 days, high-tech option with USD 25,000 within 60 days (from 1 Aug 2023); retiree criteria replaced by bank statement showing USD 18,000 or guaranteed income USD 1,500 a month; professional and self-employed changes not in scope); s. 37 Immigration Act 2022 (Sustainable City Scheme added: event added; senior-living PDS property above USD 200,000 for over-50s, already in data). s. 93(18) says s. 37(b)(iii) (senior living) is deemed in operation from 27 April 2019, but the existing senior-living term and event are dated 20 Jul 2023: needs a decision. s. 59 Non-Citizens (Property Restriction) Act: residents may buy one other residential property from USD 500,000 (was USD 350,000), and s. 70 Registration Duty Act s. 14A threshold raised from USD 350,000 to USD 500,000 (purchase permission and duty for existing residents, not a residence route: noted, not taken). Second Schedule passenger fees (USD 13-60) not in scope.

title: The Finance Act 2025 (Act No. 18 of 2025)
contains: Finance Act 2025 (66 sections amending many Acts; mostly tax and other matters, not in scope). In scope: s. 13 EDB Act new First Schedule (investor USD 50,000 and USD 100,000 options with year-1, cumulative year-5 and renewal turnover targets, 60-day transfer; start-ups; ProPass/Expert Pass and young professionals and self-employed USD 50,000 (not investment routes, not taken); Family Occupation Permit USD 250,000 (already in data); retiree USD 2,000 initial and USD 24,000 a year or USD 2,000 a month (already in data); PRP after 5 years: investor MUR 15 million a year or MUR 75 million, retiree USD 200,000 (already in data), professional MUR 400,000 salary, self-employed MUR 3 million); s. 25 Immigration Act 2022 (retiree permit 10 years, PRP 20 years, retiree conversion USD 40,000 a year, investor permit 10 years, Joint Committee and NELS procedure, dependants up to 24, combined work-residence permit, annual fee per foreign worker) commencing by Proclamation; s. 49 Registration Duty Act and s. 29 Land (Duties and Taxes) Act: new duty basis for non-citizen purchases of EDB scheme property from 1 July 2026 (registration duty rate not printed; land transfer tax 10% on non-citizen-to-non-citizen transfers: term added); s. 44 Non-Citizens (Property Restriction) Act; s. 63 Smart City Regulations (smart city fee for developers, not buyers). Terms and three events added.

title: The Immigration Act 2022 (Act No. 14 of 2022)
contains: Immigration Act 2022, replacing the 1970 Act. In scope: residence status for buyers of IRS/RES/IHS/PDS/Smart City property and G+2 apartments at USD 375,000 (alone or as each co-buyer's share) (s. 8); retiree permit (s. 10); permanent residence, 20-year validity, USD 1,500 monthly income to switch to retiree PRP (s. 11); investor occupation permit 10 years, 5-working-day deemed approval, extension of 3-year permits valid on 1 Sep 2020 (s. 12); family occupation permit 10 years (s. 14); transitional saving for IRS/RES owners (s. 39); consequential amendments to the EDB Act, Citizenship Act (s. 9(4) replaced: event added), and Non-Citizens (Property Restriction) Act (residents may buy other residential property from USD 350,000: purchase permission, no new residence route, not taken). Fees and deposits only 'as prescribed' (deposit up to MUR 100,000 applies to work-permit holders, not taken). Rest: admission, temporary residence for spouses, removal, offences (not in scope). Terms added; the Act's own event (2022-07-27) already in data. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

Rest: admission, prohibited immigrants, deportation, offences (not in scope). Terms added for validity, PRP eligibility, decision deadline, PRP validity and guarantee.

title: Owner, Employment and Investment Profile of Family Offices in Singapore (written answer), 6 March 2024
contains: Written answer of 6 Mar 2024: around 1,400 SFOs awarded tax incentives at 31 Dec 2023 (already recorded); workforce mostly local, slightly more than half male, about 10% under 30, 35% 30-40, 55% over 40; most SFOs have fewer than 20 employees; SSIC codes used. Only the SFO count was in scope as context (sfo_tax_incentive_recipients); workforce shares describe SFO employees under a tax scheme that confers no residence and are not recorded.

title: Breakdown of Approved Family Offices and Assets Under Management (written answer), 5 August 2026
contains: Singapore Parliament written answer of 5 Aug 2026 (Gan Kim Yong for the PM): more than 2,000 single family offices received 13O/13U tax incentives at end-December 2025 (already extracted), families mainly from Asia Pacific then Europe and the Americas (no numbers), and Singapore's asset management industry grew 10.1% in 2025 to $6.7 trillion AUM (whole industry, out of scope). The question asked for AUM by country and pending applications, but the answer gives no such figures.

title: Family Offices Linked to Accused Persons in Singapore's Largest Money Laundering Case (written answer), 2 July 2024
contains: Written answer of 2 Jul 2024: six SFO funds with tax incentives linked to people convicted in the money-laundering case or their spouses; tax benefits withdrawn from the year of charge or conviction, earlier benefits not clawed back unless conditions breached; assets forfeited far exceed tax benefits (no figure). Already recorded as an event; no programme numbers (the tax incentive is not a residence programme).

title: Ten Foreign Nationals To Be Charged For Offences Including Forgery And Money Laundering With An Estimated Value Of About One Billion In Cash And Various Assets
contains: Singapore Police release of 16 Aug 2023 (Wayback copy): ten foreign nationals aged 31-44 arrested on 15 Aug 2023, none Singapore citizens or PRs; per-person nationality, other passports held (incl. Cyprus, Vanuatu, St Kitts and Nevis, Turkey, Cambodia, 'Dominican Republic'), cash seized, properties and vehicles under prohibition-of-disposal orders, bank accounts frozen, charges; totals (94 properties and 50 vehicles worth more than S$815 million, more than 35 accounts with more than S$110 million, cash more than S$23 million); annex photos of seized items and passports (images not in the stored HTML copy; photos, not tables). The CBI-passport link is recorded as an event; the seizure figures concern the criminal case, not a programme, and are not recorded.

contains: Programme website page 'Donation to the National Transformation Fund' (read 2 Oct 2026): contribution paid after approval in principle; fund priorities (renewable energy, eco-tourism, education and infrastructure, deep sea port; no amounts); fee box (USD 5,000 submission fee per application, USD 90,000 single, USD 95,000 family of 2-4, USD 5,000 per extra dependant, USD 750 per applicant for documents); six-step process; FAQ (age 18+, dependants: children up to 30, parents/grandparents from 55; no residence requirement; sponsor due diligence USD 5,000; approval in about 2 months and passport 3-4 months after approval). contains: Programme website page 'Post-Approval Inclusion Fees' (read 2 Oct 2026): fees only for dependants added after approval in principle (submission fee $5,000 except newborns, spouse $10,000, each other dependant $5,000, newborn up to 1 year $500), application steps, and the same FAQ as the NTF page (extracted once, from stp-cip-web-ntf-2026). title: Decreto-Lei n.º 07/2025 - Regulamentação da Nacionalidade por Investimento ou Doação (Diário da República, I Série, N.º 33, 1 de Agosto de 2025)
contains: Decree-Law No. 07/2025 (Diário da República I Série No. 33, 1 Aug 2025, 12 PDF pages; approved 10 May 2025, promulgated 28 Jul 2025, in force on publication): regulation of nationality by investment or donation (RNID). Creates the UCID (under the Justice Minister), the programme (PCID), agent licensing (unlicensed promotion fined up to USD 500,000), the National Transformation Fund and its bank account rules (BBB- rating abroad, 10% guarantee, monthly reporting, annual published audit), a Review Committee chaired by the Public Prosecutor; applicant requirements (18+, medical certificate, criminal record under 3 months, records for 5 years), deadlines (15-day preliminary review, 15-day decision after the Prosecutor's prior approval, 90 days to pay the FNT contribution, 5 days to registry, 6 months for Prosecutor's opposition), voluntary extra investment in public projects (Annex II list of 13 project areas, no amounts), military service exemption, possible exclusion of nationalities, sanctions (fine up to 20% of the investment), annual and quarterly reporting duties, ministers may change Annex I amounts. Annex I: agent licence USD 5,000 a year, due diligence and processing USD 5,000 per application, contributions USD 90,000 / 95,000 / 5,000 per extra dependant, post-approval additions USD 10,000 spouse, 5,000 other dependants, 500 newborn. Annex III: documents list. No statistics. Five Annex I amounts and two events were already in the data; all other amounts and time limits now added. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

title: FinCEN Advisory Vol. 1, Issue 2: Enhanced Scrutiny for Transactions Involving the Seychelles
contains: FinCEN advisory (March 1996) telling US banks to scrutinise Seychelles transactions after the FATF condemned the 1995 Economic Development Act, which let investors of at least USD 10 million in approved investments obtain immunity from prosecution and asset forfeiture; attached OECD/FATF press release of 1 Feb 1996 (FATF then of 26 countries; list of members). title: FinCEN Advisory Issue 2W: Withdrawal (Transactions Involving the Seychelles)
contains: FinCEN Advisory 2W (May 2003) withdrawing the 1996 advisory because Seychelles repealed the 1995 Economic Development Act (USD 10 million investors; repeal date not given); the FATF had withdrawn its warning too. Already recorded as an event; nothing else in scope.

title: Other fees (Permanent Resident, Residence Permit incl. Eden Island Scheme, Citizenship)
contains: Immigration Department fee list (2020): permanent residence permit fees by category (investors SCR 150,000; marriage, priority worker, student), ordinary residence permit SCR 150,000 for 5 years plus SCR 75,000 spouse and SCR 25,000 per child, Eden Island Scheme SCR 150,000 for 5 years incl. spouse and children, dependent permit, citizenship fees incl. special circumstances investors SCR 350,000, SCR 1,000 processing fee on all applications; plus GOP, visitor permit, civil status, ID card and passport fees (out of scope). Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

title: Application for Permanent Residence Permit (Form IMM-15), notes and instructions
contains: Form IMM-15 notes (Dec 2013): permanent residence criteria and fees for marriage, priority worker, student and investor categories; investors USD 1 million plus 1 year residence or 5 years' business association, permit fee SR 150,000 (already recorded), processing fee SR 1,000, benefits (work without GOP, 50% property sanction fee, children endorsed to 18, no free health care), documents required. Non-investor categories out of scope. All investor rules now recorded. Rules restated from other sources are now recorded from this document too (decision 8).

title: A Quick Guide to the new Seychelles Immigration Rules (November 2013)
contains: Department's quick guide (Nov 2013, 19 pages) to the 2013 amendments: permanent residence and citizenship criteria by category (marriage, priority worker, student, investor), general conditions (absence up to 1 year, no prison over 1 year, citizenship exam over 80%), rights of permanent residents and citizens, deprivation and renunciation, and fictional example cases (incl. an investor with USD 500,000 not eligible, and a USD 1.5 million Eden Island villa owner eligible only for a residence permit because a private residence is not a direct investment). Investor rules recorded (USD 1 million, 1 year residence or 5 years' association, 11 years for citizenship, exam, absence limit, sanction-fee benefit); the example amounts are illustrations, not rules, so not recorded. Images are photos only.

title: Application for Registration as a Citizen of Seychelles under Special Circumstances (Form IMM2), notes
contains: Form IMM2 notes (Feb 2014) for citizenship under special circumstances (Citizenship Act s. 5(2), 5A-5C): criteria for marriage, students, priority workers, investors (USD 1 million in a business plus 11 years' aggregate residence) and former citizens; three sponsors, newspaper and Gazette notices, 80% in the citizenship exam, no prison sentence of 1 year or more, no continuous absence of 1 year without permission, SR 1,000 processing fee. All investor-relevant rules recorded.

title: Residence Permit (web page)
contains: Immigration Department web page on the ordinary Residence Permit (captured 2026): criteria (family connection or special contribution), no right to work, proof of financial status, conditions (5 days' residence per 12 months, bank guarantee of at least SCR 20,000, no free health care or social security), processing fee SCR 1,000, permit fee SCR 150,000 for 5 years, SCR 75,000 spouse, SCR 25,000 per child. Does not mention Eden Island or any investment amount. Conditions and processing fee recorded under the Eden Island programme with a caveat; the ordinary-permit fees are not the Eden Island fees (the 2020 list prices that scheme separately) so they are not recorded.

title: Turks and Caicos Islands Commission of Inquiry 2008-2009: Report of the Commissioner, Sir Robin Auld
contains: Report of the Turks and Caicos Islands Commission of Inquiry 2008-2009 (Sir Robin Auld, 31 May 2009, 266 pp.) into possible corruption by elected members: governance, Crown Land, public contracts, political donations, payments to named ministers, aircraft, casino, recommendations (interim direct rule, criminal sanctions, integrity, Crown Land, constitution). In scope only the immigration parts: statutory scheme of Belongership, Permanent Residence Certificates (incl. investment in a business or home) and permits (paras 3.64-3.66), complaints of PRCs and Belongership granted for bribes (3.67, already an event), 2004 Immigration Review Commission (3.70-3.74), recommendation to remove ministers from grants (3.75, 5.x, rec. 62), Belonger status granted to a golf-course developer (4.95), Immigration Department inefficiency and waived work permits for developers (4.235-4.237). The report gives no counts of PRCs or Belongerships granted and no programme money figures; the dollar figures in it concern Crown Land, loans and payments to ministers and are out of scope. Immigration fees as almost 10% of recurrent revenue 2005/06 (para 3.81) cover all work permits and immigration fees, not the investor routes, so not recorded.

No statistics.
